quarterly_data.quarter: Arista press release: Arista Announces Rack-Scale Architectures for Scale-Up and (10-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Arista announced its open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio for high-density scale-up and scale-out AI infrastructure, which it says was engineered in partnership with AMD, Arm, Broadcom, d-Matrix, Meta, Microsoft and Qualcomm and leverages the Ethernet for Scale-up Networks (ESUN) initiative: liquid-cooled racks supporting up to 144 accelerators per rack and more via cross-rack architecture. It introduced Etherlink SU-144, an Ethernet-based scale-up architecture that expands unified computing domains up to 144 accelerators (XPUs) in a single-hop network and scales to 1,024 XPUs through cross-rack topologies, in three form factors: an orthogonal chassis (single-hop, single-rack, 100–400kW liquid cooling support), a cabled backplane, and a cross-rack system. The scale-out rack designs support ESUN, Nvidia's NVLink, NVLink Fusion or PCIe as scale-up protocols, run Arista EOS or an open NOS, and feature multiple liquid-cooled 7060EX7 switches (102.4 Tbps capacity per switch), fiber patch panels, liquid-cooling manifolds and power shelves with Backup Battery Units (BBU). The release states no availability or shipment date.
quarterly_data.figure: Etherlink SU-144: up to 144 XPUs single-hop per rack, 1,024 XPUs cross-rack; 100–400kW liquid cooling support; 7060EX7 at 102.4 Tbps per switch

quarterly_data.quarter: Arista press release: Arista Announces Rack-Scale Architectures for Scale-Up and (10-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Arista says its rack-scale solution fully integrates switches, optics, liquid cooling and rack control and scales to higher rack capacity with next-generation optics such as XPO and open CPO/NPO: compared to today's OSFP-based switches, which deliver 1.6 Pb/s per rack, next-generation optics increases that to 6.5 Pb/s per rack, which the company says translates to nearly a 50% reduction in the overall data center footprint.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6 Pb/s per rack (OSFP-based switches) vs 6.5 Pb/s per rack (next-generation optics); nearly 50% data center footprint reduction
